title: Cowpea (Vigna unguiculata) cultivar, pest, disease and crop management trials in Brazil, one record per measured value
description: Fixed output format for every extractor and every blind transcriber. Each document gives one JSON object {trials, tables, records, end_checklist}. trials holds the context of each trial once. tables is the inventory of every table, figure and text block with values (page, label, data_cells, transcribed, skipped_reason, table_level_labels), with its cell count closed; table_level_labels carries what holds for the whole table once, starting with its axes and with inherited_context, which says once per table where each inherited field (unit, statistic, stage, target, pathogen and rhizobial inoculation) is declared; columns[] carries what holds for each measured column, including when it was measured, which is always declared. Every record points to its trial_id, table_id and column_id and inherits from all three; the effective value of a field is the record's, else the column's, else the table's, else the trial's, and a record repeats none of them unless its cell differs. end_checklist closes the inherited context per trial, the labels and footnotes per table, the axes and rows, the stage per column, two answers per column (when the methods say it was measured, whether it measures damage), one sample record per table with every inherited field resolved and checked on the page, the doses resolved per treatment with both dose forms, the counted applications (one included) and the uniform sprays and inoculant kept out, the target of each trial and the cell totals. Built from batata/schema.json v8.0 with the changes in batata/RODADA.md ('O que mudar na próxima rodada') and the context-cascade lessons of saude-piloto and pesca-piloto, listed in changes_from_batata_v8; the earlier rounds' lessons are already in v8. Source PDFs and record pages are in sources.json.
rules: 1 SCOPE. Inventory and transcribe every page of the document, except when sources.json gives extract_pages for it. Then only those pages go to tables[] and records[]; the rest is read only to fill context.

2 INVENTORY FIRST. Before writing any record, render every page and list every table, figure and text block with values in tables[], in page order, with table_id, page, label, kind and the number of data cells. Tables printed sideways on a portrait page are read from the rotated rendered page (sources.json notes says which documents have them). At the end fill transcribed and skipped_cells. For each entry: data_cells = transcribed + skipped_cells, and transcribed = number of records with that table_id. A document is not finished until every entry closes.

3 BLOCK WITHOUT NUMBER. A block printed under or beside a numbered table with its own caption line or its own header row (a second season, sowing date or experiment printed below 'Tabela 3' without a number of its own) is its own tables[] entry: label = the numbered label plus ' (bloco 2)', its own columns[] and its own trial when it is another trial. It is never joined to the block above, and its rows are never renumbered as rows of that block. Closed example, potato menschoy1974, Quadro 5 (p6): the March 1974 block below the October 1973 block had its own header; one side joined the two and renumbered 12 records (29 fields).

4 Read numbers from the rendered page, not only from the text layer. The printed page is the source; the text layer of old scans has wrong characters ('Produtiv1dade', '19B9' for 1989), and some PDFs have an encoded text layer that reads as random letters.

5 TRIALS FIRST. One trials[] entry per trial: per site, per season (safra das águas or período chuvoso, safra da seca or safrinha, cultivo irrigado no período seco, cultivo de vazante are different seasons), per sowing date block, per year, per experiment number and per environment (field, greenhouse pots, growth chamber, laboratory, storage). A document with one experiment has one trial. A cultivar or line network (VCU, ensaio de valor de cultivo e uso, ensaio regional) printed with one column block per site or year gives one trial per site or year. Rainfed and irrigated versions of the same test are two trials, unless the water regime is a factor inside one experiment (then it is a treatment). A column or row of means across trials ('Média', 'Média dos locais', 'Média dos anos', 'Conjunto', 'Análise conjunta') gets its own trial with study_kind = 'joint_analysis' and pooled_from listing the trial_ids it pools; a column of separate experiments printed side by side is not a joint analysis. Grain quality measured on the harvested grain (protein, cooking time, 100-grain weight) stays in the field trial; grain kept in storage and measured over months, or a bioassay with Callosobruchus maculatus on grain of each cultivar or treatment, is its own trial with environment storage or laboratory; a greenhouse screening of genotypes inoculated with a virus is its own trial with environment greenhouse_pots.

6 Fill each trial context field once, from wherever the document prints it (methods, caption, footnote, another table, a soil or weather table, the abstract), and put the page in context_source_pages. Use null only when the document prints it nowhere. Never take location from the authors' affiliation or the publisher's address: location is where the trial was run, as printed ('Campo Experimental da Embrapa Meio-Norte, Teresina, PI', 'Bom Jesus, PI', 'Campo Experimental Serra da Prata, Mucajaí, RR', 'Petrolina, PE'). affiliation is the institution that ran it, when printed with the trial. Write long context (application_stages, uniform_sprays, design_notes, base_fertilization, rhizobial_inoculation, cropping_system) in our own words: a copy longer than 15 words gets cut at merge.

7 INHERITED CONTEXT IS DECLARED ONCE. A record inherits six things it never repeats: unit, statistic, crop_stage, biotic_target, pathogen inoculation and rhizobial inoculation. Each one is declared once, at the level where it holds, and table_level_labels.inherited_context says, for every results, figure_labeled and text entry, where: scope 'table' = one value for every column and row of the table, written there with page and place; 'per_column' = each columns[] entry holds its own; 'per_row' = it varies by row and is part of each record's treatment (inoculated vs non-inoculated plots) or its record field; 'as_trial' = the trials[] value holds for the whole table (inoculation only); 'not_printed' = searched in header, caption, footnotes, methods and text and not there; 'not_applicable'. Record fields for these six stay null unless one cell differs from what its column, table and trial declare. Why: in the health, fishing and potato rounds one misread rule spread to every record of a document (330 records without the rate denominator in coura1987, 324 without unit in rodriguez1984, 99 cells with the wrong stratum in camargo1984, 97 records without stage in potato wolter2025). Declared once, a misreading is one wrong declaration the checker can see, not hundreds of wrong records.

8 ONE SAMPLE RECORD PER TABLE. After writing the records of each results, figure_labeled or text entry, take its first record, resolve each inherited field (record, else column, else table, else trial) and check it against the printed page of that cell: unit, statistic, crop_stage, biotic_target, pathogen inoculation, rhizobial inoculation, and also trial_id and treatment. Write the check in end_checklist.inheritance_samples, with the resolved value and the level it came from for each field. When one is wrong, fix the declaration where it lives (column, table or trial), never record by record, say what changed in fix_applied, and check a second sample, the last record of the table. A table is not finished until its sample matches the print.

9 TABLE AXES BEFORE RECORDS. For every results, figure_labeled and text entry, before any record, fill table_level_labels.row_identity.axes: what the rows are (row_factors, in the printed order), what the columns are (column_axis_kind), the factor on the columns when there is one (column_factor), and whether the table prints only the main effects of a factorial (main_effects_only). column_axis_kind: variables = each column is a measured variable (the usual); evaluation_times = the columns are the same variable at several times (CPSMV symptom score at 7, 14 and 21 days after inoculation; aphids per plant at weekly dates; emerged weevils after 30, 60 and 90 days of storage), one columns[] entry per time with its own crop_stage; classes = the same variable in several classes (grain size or sieve classes, damage categories of pods or grains, nodule size classes, % of genotypes per reaction class), one columns[] entry per class with columns[].class_label, the treatment unchanged; trial_blocks = column blocks are sites, years, seasons, sowing dates or water regimes that are separate trials, one columns[] entry per block and variable, each record taking the trial of its block; treatment_factor = the columns are levels of a treatment factor (inoculated and non-inoculated, with and without irrigation, N rate across the columns, cultivar across the columns), one columns[] entry per level and variable with the level in columns[].factor_level, and each record's treatment joins the row label and the column level with ' x ' in the printed order. A text entry has one column per variable and puts the factor level in the treatment.

10 MAIN EFFECTS ONLY, AND ONLY WITH A FACTORIAL. When the methods describe a factorial and the table prints only the mean of each level of one factor averaged over the other (or a block for each factor, 'Efeito de cultivares' and 'Efeito de doses'), main_effects_only = true and every record of the table has is_marginal = true, with treatment = the level as printed and treatment_type = the class of that level's factor. Wheat chagas2026, Tabela 5: blast incidence by cultivar and by sowing date as separate main effects, all is_marginal = true. Tomato togni2009, Tabela 3: natural enemies under the organic and the conventional system averaged over the planting arrangements; is_marginal = true. A split table ('Desdobramento', one factor within each level of the other) is not main effects: its cells are factorial cells, is_marginal = false. Negative example, closed: potato daniels2002, Tabelas 2 and 3: the rows are seed lots from farm fields in a survey, with no factorial behind them; they are survey rows with is_marginal = false (one side marked them as main effects in 46 fields). Rows that are sites, farms, lots, dates or accessions of an observational study are never marginal.

11 TABLE LABELS, THEN COLUMNS. After the axes, read the caption, the column headers, the row stub and every footnote and fill table_level_labels once (statistic and statistic_stated with page and place, transformation_stated, treatment_type of the ordinary rows, row_identity, inherited_context, letters_meaning and significance_test, scale_meaning, source_inconsistency for the whole table). Then fill columns[]: one entry per measured column with header, variable_standardized, unit and where it was read, organism_stage, plant_part, biotic_target, factor_level, class_label and when it was measured. The records inherit from the column, then from the table, then from the trial.

12 UNIT FROM HEADER, CAPTION, FOOTNOTES AND METHODS. A column's unit is read from its header, the caption, every footnote, the methods and the text, in that order, and unit_source_place says where. A unit stated only in the methods ('a produtividade de grãos foi corrigida para 13% de umidade e expressa em kg/ha', 'massa de 100 grãos, em gramas') goes to every column it describes: in the wheat round 117 fields of one document lost a unit that was printed only in the methods. A footnote that gives a unit or a scale goes to every column it points to. List every footnote of every results, figure_labeled and text entry in end_checklist.table_footnotes, with what it says and the columns it went into. unit_source_place = not_printed only after header, caption, footnotes, methods and text were searched; indices and scores are often printed without unit, and then the unit stays null. A moisture basis printed with the yield ('13% de umidade') goes in columns[].notes.

13 WHEN IT WAS MEASURED, PER COLUMN, FROM THE METHODS TOO. Every columns[] entry declares crop_stage_status. When the time is printed anywhere (header '45 DAS', '7 DAI', caption 'no florescimento', footnote, methods 'avaliações aos 15, 30 e 45 dias após a inoculação', 'contagem de nódulos aos 35 dias após a semeadura, no início da floração', 'colheita aos 70 dias'), crop_stage holds it with its page, crop_stage_source_place and crop_stage_refers_to; when it is printed nowhere the status is not_printed; when the column has no time it is not_applicable. The methods are read for the time of every column, one column at a time, and end_checklist.column_answers records for each column whether the methods say when it was measured: closed example, potato wolter2025 (p4): leaflets detached 40 days after planting and rated after six days of incubation; one side left the 10 columns of the two leaflet tables without a time (230 fields). And the other way round: the calendar of one variable never goes to another. Closed example, potato resende1987: the sampling calendar of the insects was given to the leaf-hole columns, which the methods time differently (40 fields). A table whose columns were measured at different times gives each column its own stage. A record carries crop_stage only when one cell differs from its column; when the rows are evaluation dates, each record carries its own crop_stage.

14 NEVER INVENT A STAGE. crop_stage holds only a time the document prints. A grain yield, pod, 100-grain weight, protein or cooking column takes a harvest stage only when the document prints the harvest with a date, a day count or a stage ('colheita aos 75 DAS', 'colhido em 20/06/2010', 'quando 90% das vagens estavam secas', 'colheitas semanais de vagens verdes a partir dos 45 dias'); then crop_stage is that text and crop_stage_refers_to harvest. When the document only says the grain was harvested ('na colheita', 'após a colheita') without date, count or stage, the column is crop_stage_status not_printed: the moment is not printed, only the event. Never write 'na colheita' because yield is obviously measured at harvest. Closed example, wheat silva1991 and salvadori1999 (156 fields between the two sides). end_checklist.columns counts the harvest-stage columns and each must print the harvest.

15 EXCEPTIONS ARE WRITTEN, NEVER LEFT EMPTY. A record field left null inherits from its column, table or trial in silence, so a null where the row differs looks right and is wrong. Before writing records, list in row_identity.special_rows every row whose class differs from the table (Testemunha, controle absoluto, testemunha nitrogenada, controle positivo, Média, a program row in a table of single products, a susceptible check cultivar in a table of lines) and in columns[] every column whose statistic or transformation differs. Every record of a special row carries treatment_type; every column that differs carries its own statistic or transformation_stated.

16 statistic_stated is true only when the document says what the number is, for that table: caption or footnote 'Médias seguidas...', 'média de quatro repetições', 'Média geral', 'total', a methods sentence that names the table. A footnote that only explains the letters ('Médias seguidas pela mesma letra...') does say that the cells are means: statistic_stated = true with statistic_source_place = 'footnote'. Otherwise statistic is 'mean' only when the table is a treatment-means table by context, and statistic_stated is false.

17 Percentages and relative values computed by the authors against a check (eficiência de controle %, % de controle (Abbott), redução de oviposição em relação à testemunha, produtividade relativa, perda %, eficiência relativa da inoculação) get statistic = 'relative_to_check'. statistic_stated = true when the header or footnote says what it is relative to; the formula goes in columns[].notes. Never recompute them. A difference between two printed columns that the authors print is data with statistic 'other' and the formula in columns[].notes. A share of grains or pods in one class is statistic 'percentage_of_total'.

18 One record per data cell that holds a measured value. A table with 20 lines and 6 measured columns gives 120 records. A factorial table gives every cell of every combination (all cultivars x both water regimes, all strains x every soil). A class table gives one record per treatment and class.

19 MARGINAL ROWS AND COLUMNS. Marginal rows and columns printed in the table are data cells and are always recorded, with their letter when there is one: Média, Médias, Média geral, Médio, MGT, Total, Conjunto, Análise conjunta. Set is_marginal = true and treatment to the printed label ('Média'). A mean column across sites or years is a record of the joint_analysis trial (rule TRIALS FIRST) and every record of it has is_marginal = true. Closed example, wheat ramos1976, Quadro 3: yields per year 1971 to 1974 and a column 'Conjunto'; the four year columns are four trials with is_marginal = false, and every 'Conjunto' record belongs to the joint_analysis trial with is_marginal = true. A 'Total' column that adds the classes of the same row is not marginal: it is its own variable, statistic total when the document says it is the sum. Marginal only where there is something to average over (rule MAIN EFFECTS ONLY, AND ONLY WITH A FACTORIAL).

20 Copy every number exactly as printed. value_as_printed holds the printed text without letters and without the dispersion term; value holds the number. The only allowed changes are decimal comma to point (12,5 -> 12.5) and removing thousands separators (1.083 kg/ha -> 1083 when it is a thousands point). A leading zero is kept in value_as_printed ('05') and dropped in value (5). When a point could be decimal or thousands (grain yield in kg/ha is usually thousands, '1.083' t/ha would be decimal), decide from the column's other cells and the unit, and say so in notes when it is not obvious. A table that mixes decimal commas and points keeps each cell as printed. A number printed as a word in the text ('três repetições') keeps the word in value_as_printed and the digit in value.

21 Never compute, convert, round or infer a value. No averages across rows, no sums of classes, no unit conversions (kg/ha stays kg/ha, g/planta stays g/planta, sc/ha stays sc/ha), no relative values computed from yields, no values read off a chart by eye, no value derived from a regression equation. If the document does not print the number, it does not go in.

22 ROW IDENTITY. treatment is the label printed in that table's row or column header, exactly as written, including footnote markers. When the table prints only a code ('T3', '5', 'MNC99-537F-4'), treatment = the code and treatment_code = the same code; the cultivar, product or input it stands for goes in cultivar or active_ingredient_or_input only when the document gives the key, with the page of the key in notes. When the row prints both a code and a name ('T5 - Bradyrhizobium BR 3267', '3 BRS Guariba'), treatment = the whole printed label, treatment_code = the code and the name goes in its field. Cowpea names: a released or local cultivar ('BRS Guariba', 'BRS Novaera', 'BRS Tumucumaque', 'BRS Itaim', 'BRS Cauamé', 'BRS Xiquexique', 'BRS Pujante', 'BRS Marataoã', 'BRS Paraguaçu', 'BRS Aracê', 'BR 17-Gurguéia', 'BR 14-Mulato', 'BRS Rouxinol', 'Pingo-de-Ouro', 'Sempre-Verde', 'Canapu', 'Setentão', 'Corujinha', 'IPA 206', 'EPACE 10', 'Vita 7') is a cultivar name: treatment = cultivar = the name, treatment_code null. A line or accession known only by its code ('MNC99-537F-4', 'MNC02-675F-4-9', 'TE97-309G-24', 'EVx 91-2E-2', 'CNCx 405-17F', 'IT85F-2687') is treatment_code AND treatment, cultivar null; when a line later released as a cultivar is printed by its code, it is still a code. A stub that mixes codes and names (lines with codes and checks with cultivar names) has row_label_form mixed, and each row is decided on its own by the same rule. A number that only gives the printed order or a ranking is not a code. A plot treatment number printed in its own column beside a name is treatment_code. DOSE IN THE STUB: when the stub prints the dose beside the product (a 'Dose' or 'Dosagem' column next to 'Tratamento'), the treatment is the product label and the dose joined with ' - ' in the printed order ('Lorsban 480 CE - 1,0 L/ha'), and the dose also goes to dose_and_unit; without it two rows would read the same. Closed example, potato salles1999 (42 fields). Decide all this once per table in row_identity, then write every row the same way.

23 treatment_type, closed examples. genotype = rows that differ by cultivar, line or accession, including resistance screening; fungicide = foliar fungicide sprays; seed_treatment = any product applied to the seed before sowing against pests or diseases (fungicide, insecticide), not the rhizobial inoculant; insecticide = foliar or soil insecticides applied in the crop; stored_grain_protectant = products mixed with stored grain against Callosobruchus maculatus (synthetic insecticide, inert dust, diatomaceous earth, ash); botanical = plant extracts, oils and powders used as pesticides, in the crop or on stored grain (neem, vegetable oils on grain); nematicide; spray_program = a program row that differs by the number, timing or sequence of sprays (calendar vs threshold-based), when the row is the program; biological = microbial agents against a pest or disease (Trichoderma, Bacillus, Beauveria, Metarhizium); natural_enemy = released parasitoids or predators; resistance_inducer = silicon, phosphites, acibenzolar tested as inducers; rhizobial_inoculation = rows that differ by rhizobial inoculation (strains of Bradyrhizobium, inoculant rates or methods, inoculated vs not), also co-inoculation with Azospirillum or other growth-promoting bacteria; biostimulant = growth promoters, amino acids, seaweed extracts, humic substances; herbicide; fertilizer = N, P, K, S, micronutrients (rate, source, timing, split, foliar), including the N-fertilized check of an inoculation trial; liming_gypsum; organic_amendment = manure, compost, biochar, green manure biomass as nutrient source; growth_regulator = regulators and pre-harvest desiccants; water_management = irrigation depth or ETc fraction, frequency, water deficit at a stage, rainfed vs irrigated, salinity of the irrigation water; sowing_date; spacing_density = row and plant spacing, plants per area or per hole, sowing depth; intercropping = rows that differ by cropping system or arrangement (sole cowpea vs cowpea + maize, row ratios, relative sowing times of the two crops); rotation_tillage = previous crop, rotation, cover crop, tillage system; cultural = any other management (harvest time, mulch, weeding regime, roguing); storage = storage method, container, hermetic bags, duration or temperature after harvest, when not a protectant product; inoculation_infestation = rows that differ by pathogen inoculation or pest infestation; pathogen_isolate = rows that are isolates, virus strains or pest populations; survey = rows that are sites, farms, lots or dates of an observational study; control = untreated check (Testemunha, sem aplicação, sem inseticida, sem inoculação e sem nitrogênio, grão não tratado) wherever it is printed, also the zero rate of a fertilizer trial; combination = a factorial cell crossing two classes and a marginal row that averages over two factors; other (say what in notes). SPECIAL ROWS, closed: 'Média' or 'Média geral' over two factors is combination with is_marginal = true; the mean of a column of genotypes is genotype with is_marginal = true; a positive control (a standard insecticide) keeps its product class; 'Testemunha' is control; in a rhizobial trial the N-fertilized plot is fertilizer and the plot with neither is control.

24 RHIZOBIAL INOCULATION IS A MANAGEMENT INPUT. Seed inoculation with Bradyrhizobium or another rhizobium (strains BR 3267, BR 3262, BR 3299, BR 3301, INPA 03-11B, UFLA 03-84; inoculante turfoso, líquido) is never pathogen inoculation and never goes in inoculation_or_infestation. When every plot got the same inoculant and the treatment is something else (cultivars, sowing dates, irrigation), it is trial context: trials[].rhizobial_inoculation, in our own words with strain and rate as printed, and the records carry no product or dose for it, like uniform sprays. When the document says the seeds were not inoculated, rhizobial_inoculation says that ('sem inoculação; população nativa do solo'). When inoculation is the treatment, treatment_type rhizobial_inoculation, active_ingredient_or_input = the strain as printed ('Bradyrhizobium sp. BR 3267'; two strains joined with ' + '), dose_and_unit = the inoculant rate when printed, and trials[].rhizobial_inoculation stays null. Nodulation and N-fixation columns (nodule number and mass, N accumulated in the shoot, % N from fixation) take biotic_target none and plant_part nodules or shoot, never a pest or disease. table_level_labels.inherited_context.rhizobial_inoculation says, per table, whether it holds as the trial, varies per row or was not printed.

25 UNIFORM SPRAYS ARE CONTEXT. A fungicide, insecticide or other pesticide applied the same way to every plot of a trial whose treatment is something else (cultivar or line, fertilizer, inoculation, sowing date, density, irrigation, intercropping) is not a treatment: it goes in trials[].uniform_sprays, in our own words with products, doses, number and timing as printed. For those sprays, application_method, application_stages and n_applications stay null on the trial and on the records, and active_ingredient_or_input and dose_and_unit stay null on the records. Cowpea cultivar trials often print 'controle fitossanitário com inseticidas quando necessário' or a list of products in the methods: that is uniform_sprays. Closed example, wheat chagas2026 and maciel2015 (436 fields between the two sides). When some plots get sprays and others do not (with vs without insecticide), the sprays are a treatment factor, not uniform.

26 COUNT THE APPLICATIONS, ONE INCLUDED. n_applications is the number of applications of the tested treatment. When the text or table prints it, take it. When a treatment table or calendar marks the dates, days after sowing or stages at which each treatment was applied (an X per date, a list of dates per row, 'aplicações aos 20, 30 e 40 DAS'), count them: that count is printed information, not an inference. A single application said in the methods also counts: fertilizer applied once in the sowing furrow, a seed treatment or a seed inoculation done once before sowing, one protectant mixed with the grain at storage, each is n_applications = 1 even when no table lists dates. Closed example, potato perez2001 (p2): fertilizer in the furrow, once, at planting; one side left n_applications empty in 81 fields. When the count is the same for every treated row it goes on the trial; when it differs, each record carries its own count with the page of the calendar in notes. Fill end_checklist.doses.application_count_source. Do not count when the document gives only an interval without a number or a period ('aplicações semanais durante o ciclo'): then n_applications stays null and the interval goes in application_stages.

27 CHECK AND n_applications. A null n_applications on a record means 'as the trial', so an untreated check left null inherits the applications of the treated plots. Closed rule: the untreated check in a trial with a printed or counted n_applications gets n_applications = 0 on its records, with the page that says it is untreated in notes; in a trial without a count, the check stays null like every other row. Never write 0 for a check when the trial has no count. A program row whose number of sprays differs from the trial (spray_program) carries its own n_applications.

28 DOSE RESOLVED PER TREATMENT. dose_and_unit is inherited from the methods and from treatment tables, and it is resolved for each treatment: the record takes only the product or products that treatment received and only their doses, with the page in dose_source_page. A treatment-table cell that holds the doses of several treatments, or several doses of one product used by different treatments, never goes whole into a record. Closed example, tomato mattos2002, Tabela 1 (p3): one cell printed three doses for three strategies; each strategy's records take only its own (96 fields were wrong in that document). Record each resolved cell in end_checklist.doses. dose_and_unit is null only for the untreated check, for treatments that are not products (genotypes, dates, spacings, water regimes) or when the document prints the dose nowhere; a fertilizer rate is a dose ('60 kg/ha de P2O5'), and so is an inoculant rate ('500 g de inoculante turfoso por 50 kg de sementes').

29 DOSE IN BOTH FORMS. When the treatment table or the methods print the dose of a product both as commercial product (p.c., produto comercial) and as active ingredient (i.a.), every record of that treatment carries both, commercial first, joined with '; ' ('150 mL p.c./ha; 30 g i.a./ha'), and dose_source_page is the page of the treatment table. Keeping one form and dropping the other is an error. Closed example, wheat goulart1999 (224 fields). When only one form is printed, only that one. end_checklist.doses says whether both forms were printed and how many records carry them.

30 FIXED FORM FOR PRODUCT AND DOSE. active_ingredient_or_input: the active ingredient first, as printed, then the commercial name in parentheses when the document prints it ('tiametoxam (Actara 250 WG)'); a tank mixture joins ingredients with ' + ' in the printed order; products used in alternation or in sequence by one program are joined with ', ' in the printed order; an adjuvant goes after ' + ' with its own name. The way of applying ('sistêmico', 'de contato', 'intercalado', 'alternado', 'em mistura', 'via semente', 'em cobertura') never goes in the product: it goes in notes or application_stages. Closed example, potato gomes2002: both sides wrote the alternation inside the product, each in its own way (32 fields both wrong); the right form was 'dimethomorph, mancozeb, chlorothalonil' with the alternation in notes. dose_and_unit: 'value unit' for each product in the same order and with the same joiners, commercial-product and active-ingredient doses separated by '; '. The spray volume (volume de calda, L/ha) is never part of the dose: it goes to trials[].spray_volume, or to the record's notes when it varies by treatment.

31 PATHOGEN AND PEST INOCULATION IS NOT AN APPLICATION. application_method, application_stages and n_applications describe management inputs only (insecticide, fungicide, seed treatment, fertilizer, rhizobial inoculant, regulator, biological, protectant). Inoculation or artificial infestation with a pathogen or pest (mechanical inoculation of CPSMV or CABMV on primary leaves with carborundum, releasing viruliferous Aphis craccivora, infesting stored grain with couples of Callosobruchus maculatus, sowing in soil infested with Macrophomina on purpose, spraying a spore suspension of Erysiphe) goes in trials[].inoculation_or_infestation, never in those three fields. When it is a factor of the trial (inoculated vs non-inoculated, infestation levels), it is also part of each record's treatment and the non-inoculated plots never inherit it; inherited_context.pathogen_inoculation is then per_row. Closed example, tomato charchar1998: half the seedlings were inoculated with Meloidogyne; the records are 'Mudas inoculadas x Nemadoro' and 'Mudas não inoculadas x Nemadoro'.

32 application_stages is inherited like the dose ('aos 15 e 30 DAS', 'no sulco de semeadura', 'em cobertura aos 20 DAS', 'no momento do armazenamento'). Write it on the trial when all tested treatments share it, on the record when it varies (a timing trial: each row has its own). Null when the document prints the timing nowhere, and for uniform sprays. Write it in our own words when the sentence is long.

33 RESULTS THAT LOOK LIKE DESIGN. Design and context tables give no records (rule DESIGN AND CONTEXT TABLES), with one exception: a column that varies by treatment because of the treatment is a result, even inside a table that looks like a calendar. The number of sprays a monitoring or forecasting system decided, the sprays saved, the irrigation depth actually applied under each irrigation criterion, the days each treatment took to reach a threshold: these are records (economic, water_use or the matching variable). Closed example, potato gomes2002, Tabela 1 (p2): number and dates of sprays per system; one side read it as a calendar and omitted 26 records and 8 columns. Also tomato haji1986. The test: if a different treatment would have printed a different number, and the number was not fixed by the authors before the trial, it is a result.

34 SAMPLE SIZE IS DATA. A column or line that gives how many units were assessed per treatment ('Amostras avaliadas', 'Plantas avaliadas', 'Testadas', 'n', 'Nº de grãos analisados', a line '(17) (20) (24)' under the header) is data: one record per cell, variable_standardized sample_size, statistic total. It is the denominator of the percentages beside it. Closed examples, potato daniels2002 (one side skipped 24 records; the other recorded them as other) and fishing martins2013. A fixed sample stated once in the methods ('20 plantas por parcela') is design context, not a record.

35 DESIGN AND CONTEXT TABLES are inventoried but give no records: tables that only list treatments, cultivars and lines with their origin, pedigree or grain class, strains, products, doses, spray or irrigation calendars fixed in advance, sites and sowing dates of a network, class limits, rating scales, soil analysis before the trial or weather. List them with kind = 'design', 'soil', 'weather' or 'scale', data_cells = 0, table_level_labels = null, columns = [], and use their content to fill trial and record context (a spray calendar gives n_applications by rule COUNT THE APPLICATIONS). Dose columns inside a results table are context and not data cells. A rainfall or temperature column inside a results table is weather context: skipped cells, named in skipped_reason. Soil analysis after the trial that compares treatments is a results table.

36 STATISTICS ARE NOT DATA. ANOVA and test statistics are counted as data cells but skipped, never recorded: CV, F, DMS/LSD, Tukey value, QM, GL, P > F or p-values, R2, correlation coefficients (a correlation matrix is a whole table of skipped cells), intercepts, slopes and regression equations, fitted parameters, contrast estimates, heritability, genetic parameters and adaptability or stability parameters (b1, s2d, Eberhart and Russell, Annicchiarico, AMMI scores), standard errors printed as their own row or column. A table of regression equations, an ANOVA summary or a stability-parameter table is kind 'anova', all cells skipped. A statistical-dominance table or figure (pairwise verdicts, 'difere'/'não difere', a matrix of which treatment beats which, a Scott-Knott grouping printed without the means) is kind 'anova' too. Closed example, tomato lage2011: 24 disease-progress coefficients recorded by one side were all wrong; they are skipped cells. The authors' optimum dose and the yield expected at it are data (optimum_dose); the equation that gives them is not. In a stability table, the line means are data and the parameters beside them are skipped cells. A standard error printed beside its mean in the same column block is that mean's dispersion (rule DISPERSION), not a cell.

37 DISPERSION. A dispersion term attached to one value ('± 0,5', '(2,3)', a standard error printed next to the mean) is not a separate cell: it goes in dispersion_as_printed of that value's record, and the column notes say what it is.

38 Significance letters and asterisks go in significance_letter exactly as printed, upper and lower case and spacing kept ('a', 'AB', 'a A', 'bc', '*', '**', 'ns' or 'n.s.' printed on a value). What they compare goes once in table_level_labels.letters_meaning, from the footnote. A footnote marker that points to text ('1', 'a/') stays in notes.

39 Reaction classes, traces and category lists. Cells that print a class instead of a number (I, R, MR, MS, S, T, 'Imune', 'Resistente', 'Suscetível', grain class 'Branca', 'Mulata', 'Fradinho', cooking class) are data cells: value_kind = 'class', value = null, value_as_printed = the class, variable_standardized = 'disease_reaction_class', 'pest_reaction_class' or the column's variable (grain_physical for a coat color or grain class). 'Tr' or 'traço' printed for a trace is a data cell with value_kind = 'class', value null, value_as_printed as printed. A table that lists names under category headers gives one record per name and column, value_as_printed = the category label.

40 Scores on a scale (notas 1 a 5 de sintomas de mosaico, 1 a 9 de severidade de oídio, notas de arquitetura de planta, de acamamento, de aparência de grãos) are the *_score variables or the column's trait variable, never a percentage. Write the scale and its direction once in table_level_labels.scale_meaning. A value read from a scale and printed as % of area is severity only when the header prints %.

41 Illegible cells stay in the inventory. A cell that holds a value but cannot be read with confidence is a record with value_kind = 'illegible', value = null, value_as_printed = the best reading or '', and the doubt in notes. It counts as transcribed. Never skip a cell because the scan is poor.

42 Cells with '-', '--', '–', 'NR' (não realizado), 'nd', '*' alone or blank are not data cells and are not counted. A printed 0 or 0,0 is a value and is recorded. Footnote markers on a value ('2,4¹', '13,11a/') are not part of the value: keep them in notes; asterisks that mark significance go in significance_letter.

43 Dates as values. A cell that prints a date as the measured value (flowering date '12/jun', date of first pod) is a data cell: value_kind = 'class', value = null, value_as_printed = the date as printed, variable_standardized = the column's variable (phenology_days or stand_or_emergence), and the year comes from the trial. Never convert it to days.

44 Fraction cells 'x/y' give two records: numerator and denominator, both with statistic = 'total' and the same treatment and variable, notes 'numerator of x/y' / 'denominator of x/y'. The cell counts as 2 data cells.

45 FIGURES. A figure is data only when it prints numbers at its bars or points: kind = 'figure_labeled', those numbers are records, and its columns[] are the plotted series. Read each number next to its own bar and its own axis category, and check the check bar separately. A figure without printed numbers at the points (a progress curve, a regression plot, bars without labels, a weather chart) is kind = 'figure_unlabeled' with trial_ids = [], table_level_labels = null and columns = []; every coefficient, equation term and R2 it prints is a counted cell, skipped. A figure with nothing printed has data_cells = 0 and skipped_reason 'no printed values'. Values are never read off the axis by eye.

46 TEXT VALUES. A per-treatment value stated only in the body text is mandatory when no table or labeled figure prints it. Use table_or_figure = 'text', quote at most 15 words in notes, and add one tables[] entry per page with label 'text', counting those values. A value repeated in the text from a table is not recorded again. Summaries across treatments ('a produtividade variou de 800 a 1.500 kg/ha') are optional and, when recorded, also counted. A text entry also gets a columns[] entry per variable it states. TEXT THAT CONTRADICTS A TABLE IS NOT A RECORD: when the text groups, ranks or quotes the treatments of a table differently from what the table prints, the table value is the record and the text goes in source_inconsistency (rule CONTRADICTIONS), never as records of its own. Closed example, potato daniels2004 (p4): the text grouped the genotypes by PVY resistance in a way that does not match Tabela 2; one side wrote the text groups as 20 extra records and left 18 conflicts unmarked.

47 CONTRADICTIONS. When the document contradicts itself (text vs table, caption vs footnote, two tables, the caption's year vs the methods' sowing date, methods vs number of rows, Portuguese vs English abstract, a mean that does not match its rows, a total below one of its parts), record the value from the table and fill source_inconsistency with both versions and pages. Put it on the record when it is about that value, on table_level_labels when it holds for the whole table, on the trial when it is about trial context. Do not choose or correct.

48 TRIAL OF A RECORD. A record's trial_id must be one of its table's trial_ids. When the table has one trial_id, every record of it takes that trial_id. When the table holds several trials (a column block per site, year, season or water regime that is a separate trial), each record takes the trial of its column block. Fix the trial structure in trials[] and tables[].trial_ids before writing records.

49 PRINTED SIGNS. A negative value keeps its sign in value ('-7,41' -> -7.41). A number in parentheses in a loss table is negative only when the document says so; then value is negative, value_as_printed keeps the parentheses, notes give the page. Without that statement, value is positive and the doubt goes in notes.

50 TARGET OF THE TRIAL, AND OF EVERY COLUMN. Each trial names in trials[].biotic_target the pest, disease or disorder its treatments manage or its screening is about. Before writing the columns, answer for each trial in end_checklist.targets: does the document rate any damage, pest, disease or disorder in this trial? If yes, the trial target is not none, and every yield, pod, grain and economic column of that trial takes the trial target (the authors measure the management with it), never none. A line trial rated for virus symptoms takes the virus, or multiple when it rates several; an insecticide trial against aphids takes aphids on its yield column too. A trial whose only sprays are uniform sprays rates no pest unless it prints a pest or disease column. Then answer it again for every column in end_checklist.column_answers: does this column measure damage, a pest, a disease or a disorder? If yes, its biotic_target is that target, never none. This rule existed since the cassava round and one side still broke it (potato souza1991: internal vascular damage rated with target none, 27 fields), so it is asked per column now. Nodulation, N fixation, protein, cooking time and plant traits are not damage. none only for trials that rate no pest, disease or disorder (fertilization, inoculation, density or water regime for yield and grain only); a water-deficit trial is about drought only when the document frames it as a stress screening (then abiotic_disorder).

51 COWPEA VARIABLES. Keep dry grain yield per area (grain_yield_area) apart from grain yield per plant (grain_yield_plant), green pod yield (green_pod_yield, feijão-verde harvested as fresh pods) and green grain yield (green_grain_yield, fresh shelled grain); the moisture basis goes in columns[].notes. Yield components are never mixed: pods_per_plant (or per area, unit says which), grains_per_pod, pod_length, pod_mass, hundred_grain_weight (peso or massa de 100 grãos, in g; peso de 1000 grãos too, with the base in notes), threshing_index (índice de grãos, grain mass over pod mass). Phenology in days (floração, maturação, ciclo) is phenology_days; plant height, branches, architecture and lodging scores are plant_trait. Nodule number and nodule mass are nodule_number and nodule_mass; N accumulated in the shoot or grain, % N from fixation, ureides are nitrogen_fixation; shoot dry mass is plant_biomass. Grain quality: grain_protein, grain_minerals (Fe, Zn and other nutrients in grain), cooking_time (minutes, Mattson cooker), water_absorption (hydration, imbibition before cooking), grain_physical (size, coat color, class), seed_germination_pct and seed_vigor. Callosobruchus maculatus bioassays: pest_oviposition (eggs per grain or sample), pest_emergence (emerged adults, count or %), pest_biology (development period, longevity, sex ratio), grain_mass_loss_pct (weight loss of grain), susceptibility_index (Dobie index, as printed), repellency_pct (preference and repellency tests), pest_mortality_pct. Intercropping: intercrop_index (land equivalent ratio, IEA, ATER, competitive ratio, as printed) and companion_crop_yield for the yield of maize, cassava or another crop in the same plots. Disease variables take the disease from the column's biotic_target and the organ from plant_part: severity, score, incidence, index and AUDPC are never mixed. Virus incidence by symptoms is disease_incidence_pct (target cpsmv, cabmv, cmv or virus_complex); by ELISA or RT-PCR it is virus_detection. Pest counts keep their sample unit in unit ('pulgões/planta', 'ninfas/folíolo', 'adultos/armadilha', 'cigarrinhas/10 redadas') and the stage in organism_stage; never convert units. Water: water_use for irrigation depth, evapotranspiration and water-use efficiency; plant_water_physiology for leaf water potential, relative water content, stomatal conductance, photosynthesis and transpiration. other should stay under 1%.
52 page is the PDF page number counted from 1 (first page of the file = 1), not the number printed on the page. Proceedings and journal PDFs start at printed pages like 86, 108 or 154.
53 When one column mixes several things ('Vagens/planta / Grãos/vagem', 'Nota / %'), split into separate records with the matching variable and column.
54 notes, source_inconsistency, design_notes, uniform_sprays, rhizobial_inoculation and every other text field quote at most 15 words of the document.

55 END-OF-TRANSCRIPTION CHECKLIST. Before closing, fill end_checklist. context: one entry per trial and per field in its enum (dose_and_unit is 'filled' only when every non-check product record has its own resolved dose, in both forms when both are printed, or the dose is printed nowhere for it; n_applications 'filled' only when printed or counted, one included, and the check follows rule CHECK AND n_applications; uniform_sprays 'filled' when the trial has them, 'not_applicable' when the sprays are the treatment; rhizobial_inoculation 'filled' when the trial says whether and how seeds were inoculated, 'not_applicable' when inoculation is the treatment; inoculation_or_infestation 'filled' when the trial was inoculated or infested with a pathogen or pest and the three application fields hold no inoculation; trial_label only when the document has more than one trial). footnotes: one entry per results, figure_labeled or text entry and per label. table_footnotes: every footnote of those entries and the columns it went into. rows: one entry per results, figure_labeled or text entry with the axes, the row_identity counts, the records with code and with name, the special-row records that carry their class and the marginal records; rows_match is true only when they agree. columns: the stage status counts of its columns, the harvest-stage columns (each must print the harvest), the columns whose unit came from the methods or text and those with no unit anywhere, whether the methods were searched, the columns whose statistic or transformation differ from the table and the records with a valid column_id. column_answers: one entry per column of those entries, with the two answers of rules WHEN IT WAS MEASURED and TARGET OF THE TRIAL. inheritance_samples: one entry per results, figure_labeled or text entry (rule ONE SAMPLE RECORD PER TABLE). doses: one entry per trial with product treatments, inoculant, fertilizer or uniform sprays, with the multi-dose cells resolved, whether both dose forms are printed and carried, where the application count comes from and whether uniform sprays and a uniform inoculant were kept out of the records. targets: one entry per trial with the answer to rule TARGET OF THE TRIAL and the production columns that took the trial target. totals: the sums over tables[] and the record count, with every_table_closes true only when each entry closes.

trials.description: One entry per trial (site x season x experiment x environment) in the pages in scope, plus one per joint-analysis block.

tables.description: Inventory of every table, figure and text block with values in the pages in scope, in page order.

trial_id.description: Short id unique inside the document: 't1', 't2', ... in order of first appearance.

trial_label.description: How the document names this trial when it has several ('Ensaio sequeiro', 'Ensaio irrigado', 'Safra 2014', '1ª época', 'E3', 'Cruz Alta', 'Conjunto'). Null when the document has one trial.

study_kind.description: experiment = imposed treatments; observational_survey = sampling of natural conditions with no imposed treatment (disease monitoring in farmers' fields, trap monitoring); joint_analysis = a block of means pooled across other trials of the document (a Média column across sites, 'Conjunto' across years).

pooled_from.description: For study_kind = joint_analysis, the trial_ids pooled. Empty array otherwise.

environment.description: field = open field, rainfed or irrigated, including cages and screens in the field; greenhouse_pots = casa de vegetação or telado with pots, trays or Leonard jars; growth_chamber = controlled environment; laboratory = seed health tests, plates, insect bioassays on grain or leaves; storage = grain kept in containers and measured over time (weevil damage, losses, germination after storage) as a trial of its own. Lab analysis of field samples (protein, cooking time, 100-grain weight) stays in the field trial.

water_regime.description: rainfed = sequeiro, não irrigado; irrigated = irrigation applied to the whole trial (aspersão, gotejamento, pivô, sulco). Null when the document does not say, when irrigation or water deficit is the treatment, or for laboratory and storage trials.

tillage_system.description: no_till = plantio direto, semeadura direta; conventional = preparo convencional (aração, gradagem); minimum_tillage = cultivo mínimo. Null when not printed or when tillage is the treatment.

previous_crop.description: Crop or vegetation before the cowpea as written ('milho', 'pousio', 'mandioca', 'vegetação nativa de cerrado'). Null when not printed or when the previous crop is the treatment.

cropping_system.description: Cropping system of the whole trial when it is not the treatment, as written or in our own words ('monocultivo', 'consorciado com milho, uma linha de caupi entre duas de milho', 'em aleias de leucena'). Null when not printed or when intercropping is the treatment (treatment_type intercropping).

location.description: Where the trial was run, municipality/state as written ('Teresina, PI', 'Campo Experimental da Embrapa Meio-Norte, Teresina, PI', 'Bom Jesus, PI', 'Boa Vista, RR', 'Petrolina, PE', 'Belém, PA'), farm or station name kept when printed. Never the authors' address.

affiliation.description: Institution that ran the trial, when printed with the trial ('Embrapa Meio-Norte', 'Embrapa Roraima', 'IPA' for a site of a network). Null otherwise.

season_or_year.description: Season or year as written ('2010', 'safra 2008/2009', 'período chuvoso de 2011', 'safrinha', 'cultivo irrigado no período seco', 'vazante').

sowing_date.description: Sowing date as written ('semeadura em 12/03/2010', '15 de fevereiro de 2008'). For sowing-date trials leave null; the date is the treatment and goes in the treatment of each record.

harvest_date.description: Harvest date, day count, stage or period as written ('colheita em 05/06/2010', 'aos 70 dias após a semeadura', 'quando 90% das vagens estavam secas', 'colheitas semanais de vagens verdes'), and a pre-harvest desiccation when printed. Null if not printed.

cultivar.description: Cowpea cultivar of the whole trial as written ('BRS Guariba', 'BRS Novaera', 'BR 17-Gurguéia', 'Sempre-Verde'). Null when the genotype varies inside the trial (then on each record).

biotic_target.description: Pest, disease or disorder the treatments of this trial manage or the screening is about (rule TARGET OF THE TRIAL, AND OF EVERY COLUMN). aphids = pulgão-preto (Aphis craccivora) counted or managed as pest or virus vector; whitefly = mosca-branca (Bemisia tabaci); cowpea_weevil = caruncho (Callosobruchus maculatus) in stored grain, also Zabrotes; pod_borers = broca-das-vagens and manhoso (Chalcodermus bimaculatus, Etiella zinckenella, Maruca vitrata, Thecla), any insect boring pods or grains in the field; leafhoppers = cigarrinha-verde (Empoasca kraemeri); thrips = tripes (Frankliniella schultzei, Caliothrips, Megalurothrips); leaf_beetles = vaquinhas (Diabrotica speciosa, Cerotoma arcuata); caterpillars = lagartas (Spodoptera, Anticarsia, Urbanus, Elasmopalpus lignosellus lagarta-elasmo); stink_bugs = percevejos (Nezara, Crinocerus); leafminer = mosca-minadora (Liriomyza); mites = ácaros; soil_pests = corós, cupins, larvas de solo; other_pest = any other insect; cpsmv = mosaico-severo (Cowpea severe mosaic virus); cabmv = mosaico-do-pulgão, mosaico-da-vagem (Cowpea aphid-borne mosaic virus); cmv = mosaico-do-pepino (Cucumber mosaic virus); golden_mosaic = mosaico-dourado (Cowpea golden mosaic, begomovirus); virus_complex = viruses rated together or mixed infections without naming one; other_virus = any other virus (SBMV, CMeV); powdery_mildew = oídio (Erysiphe polygoni); web_blight = mela (Thanatephorus cucumeris, Rhizoctonia solani on leaves); root_stem_rots = podridão-cinzenta-do-caule (Macrophomina phaseolina), podridão-do-colo (Sclerotium rolfsii), podridão de raiz por Rhizoctonia, Pythium, Fusarium solani, tombamento; fusarium_wilt = murcha-de-fusário (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. tracheiphilum); cercospora_leaf_spot = mancha-de-cercospora; rust = ferrugem (Uromyces); anthracnose = antracnose (Colletotrichum); scab = sarna (Sphaceloma); other_fungal_disease = any other fungal disease; bacterial_blight = crestamento-bacteriano, mancha-bacteriana (Xanthomonas); seed_or_grain_fungi = fungi on seeds or stored grain found in a health test (Aspergillus, Penicillium, Fusarium); nematodes = Meloidogyne and others; weeds; drought = water deficit screened or managed as a stress (only when the document frames it so); other_abiotic = salinity, heat, low P, aluminium, only when the treatments aim at it or the screening is about it; multiple = the treatments manage several targets at once (an insecticide program rated for aphids, thrips and whitefly); none = the trial manages and rates no pest, disease or disorder (fertilization, rhizobial inoculation, density, sowing date, irrigation or intercropping for yield and grain only).

inoculation_or_infestation.description: How a pathogen or pest got there, as written or in our own words: 'infecção natural', 'inoculação mecânica do CPSMV nas folhas primárias com carborundum', 'plantas infestadas com pulgões virulíferos', 'grãos infestados com cinco casais de Callosobruchus maculatus', 'solo infestado com Macrophomina'. Never the rhizobial inoculant (rhizobial_inoculation), never in application_method, application_stages or n_applications (rule PATHOGEN AND PEST INOCULATION IS NOT AN APPLICATION). Null if not printed.

rhizobial_inoculation.description: Rhizobial inoculation of the seeds of the whole trial when it is not the treatment, in our own words with strain, inoculant type and rate as printed ('sementes inoculadas com Bradyrhizobium BR 3267, inoculante turfoso'), or that seeds were not inoculated ('sem inoculação; rizóbios nativos'). Trial context like uniform sprays (rule RHIZOBIAL INOCULATION IS A MANAGEMENT INPUT): records carry no product or dose for it. Null when not printed or when inoculation is the treatment.

application_method.description: How the management treatments were applied, as written or in our own words ('pulverizador costal', 'tratamento de sementes', 'no sulco de semeadura', 'em cobertura', 'misturado aos grãos armazenados', 'via água de irrigação'). Never the pathogen inoculation, never a uniform spray or uniform inoculant of a trial whose treatment is something else. Null if not printed.

spray_volume.description: Spray volume of the whole trial as printed ('200 L/ha', '300 L de calda/ha'). It never goes in dose_and_unit. Null if not printed or not a spray trial.

application_stages.description: Timing of the tested treatments, shared by all of them, in our own words when the sentence is long ('aos 15, 25 e 35 DAS', 'na semeadura e em cobertura aos 20 DAS', 'no início do armazenamento'). Null when it varies by treatment (then on the record), when it is printed nowhere, or when the only sprays are uniform sprays. Never the inoculation timing of a pathogen.

n_applications.description: Number of applications of the tested treatments shared by all treated plots, when printed as a number or countable from a list or calendar, one included (rule COUNT THE APPLICATIONS, ONE INCLUDED). The untreated check is handled on its records (rule CHECK AND n_applications). Null when it varies by treatment (then on the record), when printed nowhere, or when the only sprays are uniform sprays.

uniform_sprays.description: Insecticides, fungicides or other pesticides applied the same way to every plot of a trial whose treatment is something else (cultivar, line, fertilizer, inoculation, sowing date, density, irrigation, intercropping), in our own words with products, doses, number and timing as printed ('inseticidas contra pulgões e mosca-branca quando necessário, em todas as parcelas'). Trial context, not a treatment (rule UNIFORM SPRAYS ARE CONTEXT): application_method, application_stages, n_applications, active_ingredient_or_input and dose_and_unit stay null for them. Null when not printed or when the sprays are the treatment.

spacing_or_density.description: Row and plant spacing or density as written ('0,50 m entre linhas e 0,25 m entre covas, duas plantas por cova', '200.000 plantas/ha', 'parcela de 4 linhas de 5 m'). Null when it is the treatment or is not printed.

base_fertilization.description: Fertilization and liming applied to the whole trial and not tested, in our own words ('250 kg/ha de 05-30-15 no sulco; sem N mineral'). Null when not printed. In a fertilizer trial, only what is not the treatment.

n_reps.description: Replicates per treatment as an integer, only when printed ('quatro repetições' -> 4). Null otherwise.

design_notes.description: Design in our own words, short: 'blocos ao acaso, quatro repetições', 'parcelas subdivididas', 'parcela de 4 linhas de 5 m, área útil 4 m2'. Null if not printed. At most 15 words quoted.

context_source_pages.description: PDF page where each filled context field was found, keyed by field name ({"location": 2, "n_reps": 3, "sowing_date": 4}). Fields left null are not listed.

source_inconsistency.description: Conflict about this trial's context (site in caption vs methods, number of replicates in two places), with both versions and pages. Null otherwise.

notes.description: Anything else about the trial (soil type, weed control, weather, product harvested: dry grain or green pods), at most 15 words quoted. Uniform sprays go in uniform_sprays, a uniform inoculant in rhizobial_inoculation, not here.

table_id.description: Short id unique inside the document: 'k1', 'k2', ... in page order. A table that continues on the next page gets one entry and one table_id per page.

label.description: Label as printed ('Tabela 3', 'TABELA 2', 'Quadro 3', 'Figura 1'), or 'text' for values stated in the body text of that page. A continuation keeps the label ('Tabela 1').

kind.description: results = measured outcomes; anova = analysis-of-variance, correlation, regression-equation, fitted-parameter or statistical-dominance table (pairwise verdicts), all cells skipped; design = treatments, cultivars, products, doses, spray calendars, sites and sowing dates of a network, class limits, strains; soil = soil analysis before the trial; weather = climate data; scale = rating scale; figure_labeled = figure with printed numbers at bars or points; figure_unlabeled = figure without printed numbers; text = values from body text.

trial_ids.description: trial_ids whose values are in this entry. Empty for design, soil, weather, scale, anova and figure_unlabeled entries that give no records. A record's trial_id is always one of these.

data_cells.description: Numeric, class, trace, date or illegible data cells in the body, counted before transcription. Includes marginal means and statistic rows or columns (CV, DMS, F), and every coefficient, equation and R2 printed in a figure or table; excludes dose columns, row labels, treatment-number columns and empty, '-' or 'NR' cells. A severity-and-response rust cell ('20MS') counts as 2. 0 for design, soil, weather and scale.

transcribed.description: Records written from this entry. Must equal the number of records with this table_id.

skipped_cells.description: data_cells - transcribed. Explained in skipped_reason when above 0.

skipped_reason.description: Why cells were skipped, with counts ('CV row, 5 cells'; 'rainfall column, 7 cells'; 'regression equations and R2, 12 cells'), or why the entry gives no records ('spray calendar'). Null when skipped_cells = 0 and the entry is a results table.

table_level_labels.description: Labels decided once for the whole entry and inherited by its records. Required for results, figure_labeled and text entries; null for the others.

columns.description: One entry per measured column (or per variable row of a transposed table), decided after the axes and before writing records. Required for results, figure_labeled and text entries (a text entry has one column per variable it states); empty for the others. Each column says its variable, unit, organ, target, factor level and, always, when it was measured.

notes.description: Anything the checker needs about the table (printed sideways, continues on next page, header spans), at most 15 words quoted.

statistic.description: What the body cells of this table are, for all columns that do not say otherwise in columns[].statistic: mean, relative_to_check, total, median, single_value, percentage_of_total, other. Null only when the print does not let one decide (say why in footnote_summary).

statistic_stated.description: true when the caption, header, footnote or methods say what the cells are (see the rule); false when statistic was set from context.

statistic_source_page.description: PDF page where the statement was read. Null when statistic_stated is false.

statistic_source_place.description: Where on that page: caption, header, footnote, methods, text. Null when statistic_stated is false.

transformation_stated.description: Transformation the document says was used for every column of this table, as written. When it holds only for some columns, null here and written in those columns[].transformation_stated. The values stay as printed.

treatment_type.description: Class of the ordinary rows of this table, from the record enum (genotype for a cultivar trial, insecticide for an insecticide trial, combination for a factorial table). Every row that differs (Testemunha, Média, a program row, a positive control) is listed in row_identity.special_rows AND written on each of its records: an exception is never left null.

row_identity.description: How the table is laid out (axes) and how the rows (or columns) that name the treatments are printed, decided once before writing records and checked against them at the end.

row_label_form.description: name_only = cultivar, product or level names; code_only = codes ('T1', '5', 'MNC99-537F-4', 'TE97-309G-24') with no name in the row; code_and_name = both printed in the row or in two columns (a plot treatment number beside the cultivar); mixed = some rows are line codes and others cultivar names (lines plus named checks), each row decided on its own; level = doses, dates, rates, spacings, water regimes or times; factorial = two or more factors crossed in rows and columns; isolate = isolate, strain or population codes. An ordinal number before a name ('1 BRS Guariba', 'Ordem 1') is the printed order, not a code.

code_key_page.description: PDF page of the table or text that says what each code is (treatment table, methods list). Null when the rows are not codes or no key is printed.

rows_printed.description: Number of treatment rows printed in the table, special rows included (for a factorial, the number of row labels).

rows_with_code.description: How many of those rows print a code (an accession, line or treatment code). Ordinal numbers and ranking positions are not codes. Every record from these rows has treatment_code.

rows_with_name.description: How many rows have a cultivar or product name, printed in the row or given by the key. Every record from these rows has cultivar or active_ingredient_or_input.

special_rows.description: Each row or column whose class differs from table_level_labels.treatment_type, or that is a mean or total: Média, Média geral, Testemunha, Sem controle, Total, a susceptible standard, a spray program in a table of single products, a single factor level in a table of combinations. As printed, with its class and whether it is marginal. Every record of a listed row carries that class explicitly.

axes.description: The table's axes, declared before any record (rule TABLE AXES BEFORE RECORDS).

row_factors.description: Factors whose levels name the rows, in the printed order ('cultivar'; 'line'; 'insecticide'; 'Bradyrhizobium strain'; 'P rate', 'inoculation' for a two-factor row stub; 'evaluation date' when the rows are times). At least one.

column_axis_kind.description: variables = each column is a measured variable; evaluation_times = the same variable at several times; classes = the same variable in several classes (grain size or sieve classes, damage categories, nodule size classes, reaction classes), one columns[] entry per class with columns[].class_label; trial_blocks = column blocks are separate trials (sites, years, seasons, sowing dates, water regimes); treatment_factor = the columns are levels of a treatment factor that joins the treatment of each record.

column_factor.description: Name of the factor on the columns ('site', 'year', 'water regime', 'inoculation', 'N rate', 'with and without insecticide'). Null when column_axis_kind is variables, evaluation_times or classes.

main_effects_only.description: true when the table prints only the means of each level of one factor averaged over another (rule MAIN EFFECTS ONLY, AND ONLY WITH A FACTORIAL): every record of the table has is_marginal = true. Never true for survey, lot, site or accession rows without a factorial.

significance_test.description: Test named for the letters or asterisks, as written ('Tukey a 5%', 'Scott-Knott', 'Duncan', 'teste F'). Null if none printed.

letters_meaning.description: What the letters or asterisks compare, from the footnote ('minúsculas comparam na coluna, maiúsculas na linha', '* difere da testemunha pelo teste de Dunnett'). Null if the table has no letters or asterisks.

scale_meaning.description: Scale and direction of scores in this table ('notas de 1 a 5, 1 = sem sintomas de mosaico', 'escala de 1 a 9 do IITA para oídio'), with the page in footnote_summary if it is printed elsewhere. Null when the table has no scores.

footnote_summary.description: What the footnotes and caption say that matters for the values (means, units, abbreviations, what 'Tr' or 'NR' means, sample unit, sowing and harvest dates, class limits), at most 15 words quoted. Every footnote is also listed in end_checklist.table_footnotes. Null when the table has no footnote.

source_inconsistency.description: Conflict that holds for the whole table (caption vs footnote, methods vs number of rows, Portuguese vs English caption), with both versions and pages. Null otherwise.

inherited_context.description: Where each field the records inherit is declared, once per table, before writing records (rule INHERITED CONTEXT IS DECLARED ONCE). scope table = one value for the whole table, written here with page and place; per_column = each columns[] entry holds its own; per_row = it varies by row and goes in each record's treatment or record field; as_trial = the trials[] value holds (inoculation only); not_printed = searched in header, caption, footnotes, methods and text and not there; not_applicable. Checked on one sample record per table (end_checklist.inheritance_samples).

unit.description: Unit of the cells. per_column when columns differ (the usual for a table of several variables); table when every column shares one printed unit ('Valores em kg/ha').

value.description: The table-wide unit as printed. Null unless scope is table.

source_page.description: PDF page where the table-wide value is printed. Null unless scope is table (or as_trial with a value, then the trial's page).

source_place.description: Where on that page. Null unless source_page is filled.

statistic.description: What the cells are. It mirrors table_level_labels.statistic: table when that holds for every column, per_column when some columns say otherwise in columns[].statistic.

value.description: The table-wide statistic, same as table_level_labels.statistic. Null when scope is per_column.

source_page.description: PDF page where the table-wide value is printed. Null unless scope is table (or as_trial with a value, then the trial's page).

source_place.description: Where on that page. Null unless source_page is filled.

crop_stage.description: When the cells were measured. table only when one printed time holds for every column ('aos 45 DAS', in the caption); per_column otherwise; per_row when the rows are evaluation dates; not_printed when no column has a time; not_applicable for a lab table with no age.

value.description: The table-wide time as printed. Null unless scope is table.

source_page.description: PDF page where the table-wide value is printed. Null unless scope is table (or as_trial with a value, then the trial's page).

source_place.description: Where on that page. Null unless source_page is filled.

biotic_target.description: What the cells are about. table when every column takes one target (a table of aphid counts and the yield of an aphid trial); per_column when columns differ.

value.description: The table-wide target from the biotic_target enum. Null when scope is per_column.

source_page.description: PDF page where the table-wide value is printed. Null unless scope is table (or as_trial with a value, then the trial's page).

source_place.description: Where on that page. Null unless source_page is filled.

pathogen_inoculation.description: Pathogen inoculation or pest infestation of the plots or units of this table. as_trial = trials[].inoculation_or_infestation holds for every row; per_row = it is a factor (inoculated and non-inoculated rows), part of each record's treatment; not_applicable = natural infection or none.

value.description: Table-wide inoculation as written, only when it differs from the trial (scope table). Null otherwise.

source_page.description: PDF page where the table-wide value is printed. Null unless scope is table (or as_trial with a value, then the trial's page).

source_place.description: Where on that page. Null unless source_page is filled.

rhizobial_inoculation.description: Rhizobial inoculation of the seeds of this table's plots (rule RHIZOBIAL INOCULATION IS A MANAGEMENT INPUT). as_trial = trials[].rhizobial_inoculation holds for every row; per_row = it is the treatment or a factor (strains, inoculated vs not); not_printed; not_applicable for storage and lab tables.

value.description: Table-wide inoculation as written, only when it differs from the trial (scope table). Null otherwise.

source_page.description: PDF page where the table-wide value is printed. Null unless scope is table (or as_trial with a value, then the trial's page).

source_place.description: Where on that page. Null unless source_page is filled.

status.description: filled = value found and written; not_printed = searched the whole document (methods, captions, footnotes, text) and it is not there; not_applicable = the field does not apply (dose for a cultivar trial, sowing date for a sowing-date trial, spray volume for a fertilizer trial, uniform_sprays when the sprays are the treatment, rhizobial_inoculation when inoculation is the treatment).

page.description: PDF page where the value was found. Null unless status = filled.

status.description: filled = the document says it and table_level_labels holds it; not_printed = caption, footnotes, methods and text searched and it is not there; not_applicable = the table has no letters, no scores or no transformation.

page.description: PDF page where it is printed. Null unless status = filled.

context.description: One entry per trial and per context field in the enum.

footnotes.description: One entry per results, figure_labeled or text table and per label.

table_footnotes.description: Every footnote and note of every results, figure_labeled or text entry, with the columns it went into (rule UNIT FROM HEADER, CAPTION, FOOTNOTES AND METHODS).

rows.description: One entry per results, figure_labeled or text table: the axes and the row_identity counts against the records.

columns.description: One entry per results, figure_labeled or text table: the columns[] counts against the records, and the columns whose labels differ from the table.

column_answers.description: One entry per column of every results, figure_labeled or text entry (rules WHEN IT WAS MEASURED and TARGET OF THE TRIAL, AND OF EVERY COLUMN).

inheritance_samples.description: One entry per results, figure_labeled or text entry: its first record with every inherited field resolved and checked on the page (rule ONE SAMPLE RECORD PER TABLE).

doses.description: One entry per trial that has product, inoculant, fertilizer or input treatments with a dose, or uniform sprays (rules DOSE RESOLVED PER TREATMENT, DOSE IN BOTH FORMS, COUNT THE APPLICATIONS, ONE INCLUDED, UNIFORM SPRAYS ARE CONTEXT).

targets.description: One entry per trial (rule TARGET OF THE TRIAL).

transcribed.description: Sum of tables[].transcribed. Must equal records.

skipped_cells.description: Sum of tables[].skipped_cells. data_cells = transcribed + skipped_cells.

every_table_closes.description: true only when every tables[] entry has data_cells = transcribed + skipped_cells and transcribed equal to its records.

doc_id.description: Document id from sources.json (also the PDF file name without .pdf).

trial_id.description: trial_id of the trials[] entry this value belongs to. Must be one of its table's trial_ids; when the table has one, it is that one.

table_id.description: table_id of the tables[] entry this value was read from. Its table_level_labels apply to this record.

column_id.description: column_id of the columns[] entry of this record's table. The column's variable, unit, stage, statistic, transformation and target apply to this record.

page.description: PDF page number, counted from 1. Same as the page of the table_id entry.

table_or_figure.description: Label as printed ('Tabela 3', 'Quadro 1', 'Figura 2'), or 'text'. Same as the label of the table_id entry.

treatment.description: Row label exactly as printed in that table (cultivar, line code, product, strain, dose, sowing date, water regime, 'Testemunha', 'Média'), footnote markers included; with the stub's dose joined by ' - ' when the stub prints it (rule ROW IDENTITY). For a factorial cell, and for a column that is a level of a treatment factor, the levels joined with ' x ' in the table's order ('BRS Guariba x inoculado', 'MNC99-537F-4 x sequeiro').

treatment_code.description: Code printed in the row ('T3', '5', 'MNC99-537F-4', 'TE97-309G-24'), as written, following table_level_labels.row_identity. A released or local cultivar's name ('BRS Guariba', 'BR 17-Gurguéia', 'Sempre-Verde') is not a code; an ordinal number before a name is not a code. Null only when the row prints no code.

treatment_type.description: Null = as table_level_labels.treatment_type, for ordinary rows only. Every row listed in row_identity.special_rows carries its class here, even when it looks obvious (Testemunha is control, a Média over two factors is combination, a program row in a table of single fungicides is spray_program), and every record of a main-effects-only table carries the class of its factor.

is_marginal.description: true for marginal means or totals printed in the table (Média row or column), and for every record of a table with row_identity.axes.main_effects_only = true.

cultivar.description: Cowpea cultivar of this record as written, only when it varies inside the trial and the row or the key gives a name. A line known only by its code leaves this null (the code is in treatment_code). Null when trials[].cultivar applies.

active_ingredient_or_input.description: Product, organism, strain, fertilizer source or input of this treatment in the fixed form of rule FIXED FORM FOR PRODUCT AND DOSE: active ingredient first, commercial name in parentheses ('tiametoxam (Actara 250 WG)', 'imidacloprido', 'óleo de nim', 'Bradyrhizobium sp. BR 3267', 'superfosfato simples', 'terra de diatomácea'), taken from the treatment table or methods when the results table gives a code. Tank mixtures joined with ' + ', alternated products with ', '; the way of applying never here. Only what this treatment received; never a uniform spray or uniform inoculant. Null for checks, genotypes and non-product treatments.

dose_and_unit.description: Dose of this treatment only, resolved from the treatment table or methods (rules DOSE RESOLVED PER TREATMENT and DOSE IN BOTH FORMS), as 'value unit' per product in the order of active_ingredient_or_input, '; ' between commercial-product and active-ingredient doses when both are printed ('150 mL p.c./ha; 30 g i.a./ha', '60 kg/ha de P2O5', '1 mL de óleo/kg de grãos'). Never the spray volume, never a uniform spray. Null only for checks, non-product treatments or when printed nowhere.

dose_source_page.description: PDF page where the dose is printed; when the two forms come from different places, the page of the treatment table. Null when dose_and_unit is null.

application_stages.description: Timing of this treatment, only when it differs from trials[].application_stages ('aos 20 e 35 DAS', 'na semeadura', 'em cobertura aos 25 DAS'), in our own words when long. Never the pathogen inoculation timing, never a uniform spray. Null when the trial value applies.

n_applications.description: Number of applications of this treatment when it differs from the trial: printed as a number, counted from the treatment table or calendar, or 1 for a single application said in the methods (rule COUNT THE APPLICATIONS, ONE INCLUDED); and 0 for an untreated check in a trial whose treated plots have a count (rule CHECK AND n_applications). Never counts pathogen inoculations or uniform sprays. Null otherwise.

crop_stage.description: Null = as the column (columns[].crop_stage). Filled only when this one cell has its own time, different from its column (a survey row sampled on its own date), or when inherited_context.crop_stage is per_row. Never invented: rule NEVER INVENT A STAGE.
